# README.md

## Overview
SeleneMesh processes isolated workspaces, message streams, imports and exports. Consult each topic document for the exact rule; this overview grants no access permissions.

## Operations
The platform records activity and exposes counters. Operational indicators are not service-credit or financial-compensation terms.
documents.docs/sessions.md:
# docs/sessions.md

## Ticket lifetime
Each SeleneMesh session ticket expires 53 seconds after issuance. Being idle does not stop the expiry clock.

## Renewal authorization
A ticket may be renewed at most two times, only by its bound worker and only before the active expiry.

## Renewal spacing
At least eleven seconds must pass after issuance or the last successful renewal. A successful renewal grants another 53-second lifetime.

## Signed revocation
Receipt of a signed revocation invalidates the ticket immediately. Never retry or renew that ticket; a new one requires a fresh authorization check.
documents.docs/retries.md:
# docs/retries.md

## HTTP 429 rule
After HTTP 429, automatic retry requires Retry-After to be a nonnegative integer no greater than 75 seconds. Wait exactly the indicated interval.

## HTTP 429 exception
An absent, malformed, or greater-than-75 Retry-After prevents automatic retry; there is no fallback delay.

## HTTP 503 identity
Automatic retry of HTTP 503 requires the Idempotency-Key from the original attempt, with exactly the same key and body on retries.

## HTTP 503 timing
At most two HTTP 503 retries are permitted: the first after six seconds, the second after nineteen seconds. Without the original key, do not retry automatically.

## HTTP 401 denial
HTTP 401 must not be automatically retried and the client must not acquire broader credentials on the caller's behalf; fresh authorization must occur separately.
documents.docs/imports.md:
# docs/imports.md

## Batch identity
The complete uploaded input has a SHA-256 digest bound to its batch identifier. Reusing the identifier with changed contents is a conflict and cannot mutate the existing batch.

## Resume window
Resume an interrupted batch no later than fourteen minutes after its last accepted chunk, with the same identifier and complete-input digest. After expiry begin a new batch.

## Atomic visibility
Chunks in staging are invisible to readers and exports. After validating the entire batch, an explicit commit atomically publishes it; incomplete batches never become partially visible.
documents.docs/consumer.md:
# docs/consumer.md

## Durable application commit
Write the business effect and workspace-scoped processed-event identifier in one durable application transaction. The service does not provide exactly-once external effects.

## Acknowledgement order
Acknowledge the event only after the application transaction commits; earlier acknowledgement can lose the effect on crash.

## Checkpoint order
Move the durable checkpoint only after the server confirms the acknowledgement, not when the event is merely read.

## Replay order
After crash, reopen the same workspace stream immediately after the durable checkpoint. Process replayed events in ascending sequence before later arrivals.

## Duplicate deliveries
An event committed before a crash but not acknowledged may be redelivered. Read the durable event-identifier record, skip the duplicate business effect, then acknowledge.

## Poison events
At an unprocessable event, stop the consumer and report the sequence. Do not drop or acknowledge it or advance the checkpoint; quarantine requires a separate authorized operator action.
documents.docs/exports.md:
# docs/exports.md

## Export snapshot
An export reads the committed manifest current when its request was accepted, excluding later commits and uncommitted import chunks.

## Creation permission
Export creation requires an active ticket and read permission for the requested workspace; it grants no read permission for another workspace.

## Independent expiry limits
An export object is retained four hours, while a signed download link lasts eighteen minutes. Every download rechecks permission; revocation blocks access immediately.

## Resume and renewal
Resume with the same export identifier and byte Range, checking that the snapshot identifier matches. A renewed link requires fresh authorization and does not refresh the object's four-hour retention.
documents.docs/workers.md:
# docs/workers.md

## Worker drain
Draining a worker stops new assignments only to that worker. Its current task, sibling workers and the workspace continue.

## Workspace pause
Pausing a workspace stops new assignments to every worker in that workspace; running tasks and other workspaces continue.

## Task cancel
Cancelling a running task requires its exact task identifier, workspace identifier and explicit cancel permission; worker drain and workspace pause are not cancellation.

## Workspace resume
Resuming a workspace clears its pause flag but not a separately drained worker; that worker must be resumed explicitly.
documents.docs/security.md:
# docs/security.md

## Key rotation
Encryption keys rotate at most every thirty-nine days; newly encrypted records use the new key.

## Overlap window
For eight minutes after a planned rotation, an older key can decrypt existing records but cannot encrypt new ones.

## Revoked key
A revoked key is rejected immediately for both encryption and decryption, regardless of the planned overlap window.

## Workspace isolation
Access tokens are bound to a single workspace. No cross-workspace read is authorized by a token for another workspace.
documents.docs/quotas.md:
# docs/quotas.md

## Steady request rate
The steady API request quota is 250 requests per minute per workspace.

## Storage thresholds
At seven gigabytes, a workspace gets a storage warning; at eight gigabytes, new writes are rejected until usage falls.

## Burst rule
At most twenty requests are accepted per ten-second burst window, independently of the minute quota.
documents.docs/audit.md:
# docs/audit.md

## Audit retention
SeleneMesh keeps AuditTrail entries for thirty-three days before scheduled deletion.
